item.title: Hook, Line & Dine in New Orleans: Venice Yellowfin to a Commander’s Palace Feast
item.description: We ran offshore from Venice at dawn, boxed up Gulf yellowfin by midday, and ended the day at Commander’s Palace—where our fresh catch became a true New Orleans feast. The post Hook, Line & Dine in New Orleans: Venice Yellowfin to a Commander’s Palace Feast first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Florida Anglers Cheer Potential 39-Day Atlantic Red Snapper Season After Years of Short Closures
item.description: Anglers and fishing charter operators along Florida’s Atlantic coast are celebrating a major step toward a longer recreational Atlantic red snapper season in 2026, potentially ending years of very short seasons under federal limits. The post Florida Anglers Cheer Potential 39-Day Atlantic Red Snapper Season After Years of Short Closures first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Winter Smallmouth Love River Pockets! ❄️
item.description: As water temps drop, bass move into slower bank-side pockets and back eddies where they can rest and let the current bring food to them. Target these areas with a hair jig, fish it slow along the bottom, and use light line for better sensitivity. Give each pocket 15–30 minutes — you might be surprised how productive winter fishing can be! 🎣 The post Winter Smallmouth Love River Pockets! ❄️ first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Winter Fishing In New England – No Shanty, No Problem! ❄️🎣
item.description: Our forefathers braved brutal winters with far less gear than we have today. Thankfully, modern ice anglers come prepared! With ice starting to form up north, hardwater season is almost here. Once it sets, target the shallows, vary your lure sizes, and match your bait to local forage. Who’s ready to get out on the ice? 🧊🐟 The post Winter Fishing In New England – No Shanty, No Problem! ❄️🎣 first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.

item.title: Mutiny on the Leslie Rae (1987): Murder Aboard a Florida Shrimp Boat
item.description: In July 1987, more than 20 miles off Cape Canaveral, a routine shrimping trip aboard the Leslie Rae turned deadly. A violent mutiny left the captain dead and a first mate fighting for survival in the open Atlantic. Nearly four decades later, it remains one of Florida’s most chilling maritime crime stories. 🌊 The post Mutiny on the Leslie Rae (1987): Murder Aboard a Florida Shrimp Boat first appeared on Coastal Angler & The Angler Magazine.
